say: You have two hours and forty minutes to get off the Titanic, and you're holding a fortune that isn't yours.
show: You have 2 hours and 40 minutes to get off the Titanic, and you're holding a fortune that isn't yours.

say: April fourteenth, nineteen twelve. Eleven forty P.M. The ship just hit an iceberg.
You're Tommy. Third class. The bottom of the ship.
Ten minutes ago, a rich woman ran down to your deck, pushed a bag into your hands, and whispered:
Don't open it. I'll come back for it.
You opened it.
Diamonds. Enough to buy a whole street in New York.
Then you see it. A thin line of water, sliding under your door.
And here's what nobody on board knows yet.
The lifeboats hold one thousand one hundred seventy-eight people.
There are two thousand two hundred twenty-four on this ship.
You run for the stairs. The gate is shut.
Back to your cabins! There is no danger!
That night, many third-class passengers reached the boat deck too late.
Then she's back. But she's not here for the bag.
They know you have it. Hide it... and don't trust anyone in a uniform.
Why would a rich woman give her diamonds to me?
show: (Why would a rich woman give her diamonds to me?)

say: So, Tommy. Do you stay at the gate and wait, or run with the diamonds and find another way up?
Comment stay or run. The top comment decides Part 2. Follow, so you don't miss it.
Because the man looking for that bag... is already on the stairs.
Evening, Tommy.
